note.title: Customs, festivals and celebrations
note.specFocus: Customs, special occasions, religious and non-religious festivals, traditions, food, music, family celebrations, public events, and personal opinions.
note.sourcePages: Original GCSE Spanish revision material; it is not an official AQA paper, mark scheme, or copied publisher content.
note.summary:
Customs, festivals and celebrations

Key vocabulary
- la fiesta; la celebración; el desfile; la costumbre; los fuegos artificiales; decorar; celebrar; la Nochevieja; la boda; el cumpleaños; el disfraz; tradicional; típico/a; participar

Key grammar
- Use the present for regular customs, the preterite for one celebration, and the imperfect for background description or childhood traditions. Add comparisons and justified opinions.

Exam tips
- Use se celebra / se come for general customs. Distinguish celebrar (to celebrate) from tener lugar (to take place). Give a cultural detail, not only an opinion.

questions.examTip: Translate sense units, not isolated words, and check tense and negatives before finalising each answer.
questions.modelAnswer:
1. In my town we celebrate a spring fair every April.
2. As a child I dressed up as an animal for carnival.
3. On New Year's Eve some people eat twelve grapes at midnight.
questions.question:
Reading comprehension. Read the passage and answer in English.

“En mi ciudad celebramos una feria de primavera cada abril. De niña me disfrazaba de animal para el carnaval. En Nochevieja algunas personas comen doce uvas a medianoche.”

1. What is said in the first sentence?
2. What additional point appears in the second sentence?
3. Give the main idea of the final sentence.
